MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  DECEMBER 4, 2017

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
CHAIRMAN YOO.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIRMAN YOO led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Chair Yoo, Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott,
  Zigrang

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom,
  Planning Technician/Code Administrator Slawson

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING OF
  NOVEMBER 6, 2017.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A. WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL RESOLUTIONS THAT ARE PRESENTED FOR THE
  CONSIDERATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION ON TONIGHT’S AGENDA AND
  ALL SUCH RESOLUTIONS SHALL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER,

  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEM 6-A.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

  B. SEMI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORECEMENT REPORT – JUNE 1-DECEMBER 1, 2017

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the cases with the description, “Illicit Connection”.
  Code Enforcement Administrator/Planning Technician Slawson stated that these cases
  are Illicit discharges found due to the Public Works Department’s storm drain improvement
  project. Planning Director Wahba stated that this is where people have found a way to
  connect directly to storm drains that drain onto the canyons or the street.

  In a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Director Wahba stated that the State
  and the County are working to determine what can be drained directly onto the street.
  These cases are more of a connection from yards to laterals and then to the larger storm
  drain system.

  In a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Code Administrator/Planning Technician
  Slawson stated that currently the City is taking a more “education” approach rather than
  fines since most property owners are completely unaware that they are connected to City
  maintained infrastructure. Staff is working with property owners to correct the issues.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG inquired about the scope of work at a property on Lantana
  Place. Code Enforcement Administrator/Planning Technician Slawson stated that it is for
  a rear retaining wall that was built without permits and repair of a drainage swale.

  1
Planning Commission Minutes
December 4, 2017
   COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 6-B.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 25-17; APPLICANT: MR. AND MRS. KEITH KHOREY;
  60 DAPPLEGRAY LANE; A request to approve a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination for conversion of existing building area to habitable and non-habitable use,
  and for one and two-story additions to a split-level residence. (KT)

  Associate Planner Thom provided a summary of the staff report for Planning Application
  No. 25-17 per written material and stated that staff recommends that the Planning
  Commission approve Planning Application PA-25-17 with the conditions of approval as
  stated in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the two storage areas called out on Floor-0, are
  bedrooms. Associate Planner Thom stated that they are not bedrooms and staff required
  that the ceiling heights be lowered to less than the required height of 7 feet in order to
  prevent them from becoming a habitable space.

  Joe Spierer and Raymond Wong, Architects, provided a presentation of the proposed
  project.

  Keith Khorey, Property Owner, stated that there are several unpermitted structures and
  the proposed project will improve the property and correct the layout. In addition, there
  will essentially be no change to the front of the property. The added square footage will
  be to the rear of the property.

  David Barge, Neighbor at 62 Dapplegray Lane, stated that he is in opposition of the project
  due to privacy issues. Mr. Barge’s main concern is with the balcony and the proximity to
  his property.

  After a brief discussion, Mr. Barge, the architects, and the property owners, agreed to add
  a trellis with a “living wall” (tight vegetation) to the portion of the balcony that looks into the
  Barge property that will be installed up to the plate height. Planning Director Wahba stated
  that the back of the “living wall” must be aesthetically pleasing for the neighbors as well.
  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG added that the back should have the same siding as the rest
  of the house.

  In a question by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG, Planning Director Wahba provided an
  explanation on the “50% rule” and cautioned the architects that this project not exceed
  50%. Any deviation from what is approved may require that the project be brought before
  the Planning Commission, and will require a new application.

  COMMISSIONER  SCHACHTER  MOVED,  SECONDED  BY  COMMISSIONER
  MEDAWAR TO,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION 25-17 WITH THE MODIFICATIONS TO
  THE PROJECT AS DISCUSSED.

  Ayes: CHAIR YOO, CARMAN, EDLER, MEDAWAR, SCHACHTER, SCOTT,
  ZIGRANG
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that Planning Application 25-17 has been approved; there
  is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

  B. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 27-17; APPLICANT: URLICH BLAETTLER AND
  BARBARA NEWMAN; LOCATION: 5145 BLUEMOUND ROAD; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to demolish a portion of the existing single-
  story residence and for one-story additions to be constructed in the breezeway, side and
  rear yards. A Minor Deviation is required for a single-story addition to be built along
  existing building lines that encroaches into a side yard setback that is legally
  nonconforming.

  2
Planning Commission Minutes
December 4, 2017
   Associate Planner Thom provided a summary of the staff report for Planning Application
  No. 27-17 per written material and stated that staff recommends that the Planning
  Commission continue this application to a date uncertain to address the policy issue of the
  shed roof/clerestory window design and provide staff with director on whether the design
  meets Neighborhood Compatibility.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN inquired about the detached bedroom on the other side of
  the patio. Associate Planner Thom stated that there is a permitted detached accessory
  dwelling unit.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if properties with legal nonconforming items are typical
  of the neighborhood. Planning Director Wahba stated that approximately 50% of the
  homes meet the required 10 foot setback.

  Tarek Abdel-Ghaffar, Colega Architects, provided history on the architecture in the
  neighborhood as well as a presentation of the proposed property.

  Urlich Blaettler, Property Owner, stated that he is new to the City. Mr. Blaettler stated that
  he did research prior to buying the property, including speaking to planning and reviewing
  building permits. He also stated that he as well as the architects are communicating with
  the neighbors about the proposed project. Mr. Blaettler commended the architect and
  stated that this house fits in very well with the neighborhood.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the only reason that this item is being brought to the
  Planning Commission is for the shed roof in reference to Neighborhood Compatibility.
  Planning Director Wahba stated, yes.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she appreciates the detail given to this project
  and the communication with the neighbors.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER concurred and stated that he appreciates the communication
  with the neighbors.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that the architect did a great job and provided a great
  modern feel to the original architecture.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that this is a wonderful project and stated that there
  should be no problem with a shed roof in this project or in this neighborhood.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 27-17 AS PRESENTED.

  Ayes: CHAIR YOO, CARMAN, EDLER, MEDAWAR, SCHACHTER, SCOTT,
  ZIGRANG
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that Planning Application 27-17 has been approved; there
  is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

  COMMISSIONER YOO called a recess at 8:24 p.m. and reconvened at 8:29 p.m.

  C. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 28-17; APPLICANT: MR. GREG ANDRES; LOCATION :
  27809 CONESTOGA DRIVE; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
  for first and second story additions to an existing single-family home and to construct a
  second dwelling unit in the rear yard. A Minor Deviation is required to reduce the front
  yard area by no more than 10% and to continue a legal nonconforming west side yard
  setback.

  Code Administrator/Planning Technician Slawson provided a summary of the staff report
  for Planning Application No. 28-17 per written material and stated that staff recommends
  that the Planning Commission continue Planning Application No. 28-17 to a date uncertain
  to allow the applicant to address the Neighborhood Compatibility concerns, as outlined in
  the report.

  3
Planning Commission Minutes
December 4, 2017
   Planning Director Wahba provided background on the homes in the neighborhood that
  have some Spanish architectural characteristics. He stated that he would like to see more
  of the ranch-style characteristics come back to the neighborhood, however, this project
  would definitely allow for more Spanish style architecture.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the City has a definition of a Spanish-style home.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that something can be prepared and went on to describe
  characteristics found in Spanish architecture.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the City is bound by State law in regards to the
  City’s discretion on second dwelling units. Planning Director Wahba stated that the City
  has still elected to apply Neighborhood Compatibility requirements to second dwelling
  units.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked if the second dwelling unit could be a rental. Planning
  Director Wahba stated that it can be a rental and it is allowed by the State of California.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired to an alternative to the bridge.

  In a question by COMMISSIONER CARMAN, Planning Director Wahba stated that on any
  recent major remodels, red tile roofs will not be found and that this would be the “tipping
  point” in allowing Spanish-style architecture in this neighborhood.

  Bizhan Khaleeli, Architect, stated that this project is a Spanish-ranch architectural style.
  Mr. Khaleeli provided a presentation on the proposed project.

  Greg Andres, Property Owner, stated that he needs to expand the house and it is in need
  of renovations. Mr. Andres stated that he and his wife would really like a Spanish ranch
  home and stated that the bridge would provide accessibility to the second dwelling unit
  and the upper portion of the backyard.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT inquired about the stark unbroken two story walls in the back
  yard. Code Enforcement Administrator/Planning Technician Slawson stated that the
  architect is willing to pull back the second story to break-up the massing of the property.

  Planning Director Wahba explained that there are various forms of ranch style homes,
  however, there is a certain type of ranch style that was typical of the Larga Vista
  neighborhood.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that Larga Vista is one of the more consistent Western
  ranch style neighborhoods and there are only a couple of homes where the Spanish ranch
  style is done well, but still does not fit into the neighborhood. In addition, more detail is
  needed in order to review this proposed project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN commented that staff has made the right decision on this
  project and appreciates the desire of the property owner, but would also appreciate an
  effort to make this design more compatible with the “country” feel of the neighborhood.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he is open to the Spanish ranch style, but
  understands that this will set a precedent going forward. More detail is needed in order to
  properly review this proposal.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he would not mind a single-story “hacienda”, but
  a two story will need more details in order to make a decision. He also commented that
  the bridge is a little “bizarre”, but understands the need for accessibility to the accessory
  dwelling unit. However, more detail is also needed for the design of the bridge.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that he is concerned with the Neighborhood
  Compatibility factor and the design being compatible with existing styles, and commented
  that he is concerned with the proposed bridge.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he appreciates staff’s work on this project and
  agreed that more detail is needed, and the bridge is questionable; he would like to see
  other options.

  CHAIRMAN YOO stated that more details on the design, including the bridge, are needed
  in order for further review to be able to visualize what the final design will look like.

  4
Planning Commission Minutes
December 4, 2017
   Mr. Khaleeli stated that he would like to bring back a design that will be acceptable by staff
  and the Planning Commission, but asked for direction on what will be considered
  acceptable. COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he does not feel that Spanish ranch
  style fits in with this neighborhood. COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that the example
  on Carriage Drive is one that stands out.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the red tile is something that the applicant should exclude
  from the design. Planning Director Wahba stated that when elements are excluded and
  others added, this is what creates a confused design.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 28-17 TO A DATE UNCERTAIN,
  TO ALLOW THE ARCHITECT TO WORK WITH STAFF ON A DESIGN THAT
  WILL BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE NEIGHBORHOOD AND PROVIDE A
  DESIGN WITH MORE DETAIL.

  There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

  D.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 20-17; APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES; LOCATION: DAPPLEGRAY NEIGHBORHOOD; Survey to allow metal
  standing-seam roofs on residential homes in the Dapplegray Lanes Neighborhood and
  possible city-wide.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a summary of the staff report for Planning Application
  No. 20-17, which included the results of the survey to allow metal standing-seam roofs on
  residential homes in the Dapplegray Lanes Neighborhood. The results were split almost
  50/50 with only a slight favor to not allow metal standing-seam roofs.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the recommendation is that the Planning Commission
  discuss the results and direct staff on how the City Council may wish to proceed.

  The Planning Commission held a discussion on this item and discussed introducing a new
  type of roof option to the City.

  Keith Khorey, RHE Resident, stated that he is renovating his home and thinks that a black
  standing-seam roof is something he would consider in order to provide contrast to the
  design. Mr. Khorey added that this type of roof is compatible with the homes in the
  neighborhood.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the City should consider metal standing-
  seam roofs pursuant to HOA’s approval where applicable.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there need to be strict design regulations if standing-
  seam roofs are allowed.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if metal standing-seam roofs be introduced at out-
  buildings only. Planning Director Wahba stated that there was a time when they were
  allowed on out buildings in the Dapplegray Lanes neighborhood, but that has since
  changed.

  The Planning Commission agreed that if metal standing-seam roofs are allowed, they
  must have the HOA’s approval where applicable with strict design regulations
  implemented by the City.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved to receive and file.

  There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG inquired about the sand stockpile location walls at the Golf
  Course. Planning Director Wahba stated that they were considering this on a
  temporary basis, but may now be permanent and there were also gates installed at the
  main entrance that were not a part of the plan.

  5
Planning Commission Minutes
December 4, 2017
   Planning Director Wahba stated that the gates will be open during business hours and
  may be locked at night. These issues will need to be further addressed by the Planning
  Commission and the City Council at a later time.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  A. 2018 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULE.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the 2018 Planning Commission meeting schedule is
  provided with changes for the New Year’s Day and Labor Day holidays.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A. DRAFT MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMITTEE MEETING,
  NOVEMBER 8, 2017.

  B. DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JOINT ADJOURNED MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  AND PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION, NOVEMBER 8, 2017.

  C. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, NOVEMBER 14, 2017.

  D. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, NOVEMBER 28, 2017.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved,

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11-A THROUGH 11-D.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIRMAN YOO adjourned the meeting at 10:03 p.m. to the next the meeting of January
